sourceDoc.text:
Effect of Doxycycline on Aneurysm Growth Among Patients With Small Infrarenal 
Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

IMPORTANCE: Abdominal aortic aneurysms affect more than 3% of US older adults.
OBJECTIVE: To test whether doxycycline reduces the growth of abdominal aortic 
aneurysm over 2 years as measured by maximum transverse diameter.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Parallel, 2-group, randomized clinical trial 
that was conducted at 22 US clinical centers between May 2013 and January 2017, 
and enrolled patients 50 years or older with small (3.5-5.0 cm for men, 3.5-4.5 
cm for women) infrarenal aneurysms. The final date of follow-up was July 31, 
2018.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive twice daily for 2 years 
doxycycline 100 mg orally (as capsules) (n = 133) or placebo (n = 128).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in abdominal aortic 
aneurysm maximum transverse diameter measured from CT images at baseline and 
follow-up at 2 years. Patients were assigned ranks based on the maximum 
transverse diameter (measured or imputed) of the aorta and also if they 
underwent aneurysm repair or died. The ranks were converted to scores having a 
normal distribution to facilitate the primary analysis ("normal scores").
RESULTS: Of 261 patients randomized, no follow-up CT scans were obtained on 7 
(3%), leaving a final analysis set of 129 patients assigned to doxycycline and 
125 to placebo (mean [SD] age, 71.0 years [7.4 years], 35 women [14%]). The 
outcome normal scores used in the primary analysis were based on maximum 
transverse diameter (measured or imputed) in 113 patients (88%) in the 
doxycycline group and 112 patients (90%) in the placebo group; aneurysm repair 
in 13 (10%) and 9 (7%), and death in 3 (2%) and 4 (3%), respectively. The 
primary outcome, normal scores reflecting change in aortic diameter, did not 
differ significantly between the 2 groups, mean change in normal scores, 0.0262 
vs -0.0258 (1-sided P = .71). Mean (SD) baseline maximum transverse diameter was 
4.3 cm (0.4 cm) for doxycycline and 4.3 cm (0.4 cm) for placebo. At the 2-year 
follow-up, the change in measured maximum transverse diameter was 0.36 cm (95% 
CI, 0.31 to 0.40 cm) for 96 patients in the doxycycline group vs 0.36 cm (95% 
CI, 0.30 to 0.41 cm) for 101 patients in the placebo group (difference, 0.0; 95% 
CI, -0.07 to 0.07 cm; 2-sided P = .93). No patients were withdrawn from the 
study because of adverse effects. Joint pain occurred in 84 of 129 patients 
(65%) with doxycycline and 79 of 125 (63%) with placebo.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with small infrarenal abdominal aortic 
aneurysms, doxycycline compared with placebo did not significantly reduce 
aneurysm growth at 2 years. These findings do not support the use of doxycycline 
for reducing the growth of small abdominal aortic aneurysms.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01756833.

recordedTake.finding: Doxycycline did not reduce abdominal aortic aneurysm growth over years in this multicenter randomized trial, with the aortic diameter outcome not differing significantly from placebo.
recordedTake.designCaution: Follow-up imaging was incomplete for some patients so diameters were partly imputed, and the primary outcome was a composite rank score that blends diameter change with repair and death, which complicates direct clinical interpretation.
recordedTake.relevance: Negative RCT on medical therapy for small AAA, squarely within your AAA/TAAA outcomes north star and worth discussing at conference.

check.reason: The snippet explicitly states the primary outcome 'did not differ significantly between the 2 groups' with P=.71, and confirms equal measured diameter changes (0.36 cm in both groups, P=.93), directly supporting the claim that doxycycline did not reduce aneurysm growth compared to placebo.

cautionCheck.reason: The snippet confirms incomplete follow-up (7 of 261 patients had no CT scans), describes imputation of maximum transverse diameter, details the composite primary outcome using 'normal scores' based on diameter/repair/death rankings, and acknowledges this ranking approach was used to 'facilitate the primary analysis,' all supporting the stated methodological limitations.
